en.greeting: Hi! Today we'll learn to describe people, places and things: a red car, a busy day, a very hot afternoon. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Adjective first
steps.text: Adjectives are describing words, like big, new and cheap. Let's see where they go.
steps.body: An **adjective** describes (big, red, cheap). A **noun** names a thing, person or place (car, bag, Rina). In Indonesian the adjective comes **after** the noun: *mobil merah*. In English it comes **before**: **a red car**. **a/an** looks at the sound of the very next word: **a** new bike, **an** old bike. Adjectives never take **-s**; only the noun shows 'more than one': two **big boxes**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You're shopping at a market in Bandung.

question.prompt: You want to say 'Saya mau tas hitam.' Which sentence is correct?
question.explanation: In English the adjective goes **before** the noun: **a black bag**. 'a bag black' is Indonesian order. And 'blacks' is wrong: only the noun can take -s, never the describing word.

steps.title: be + adjective
steps.text: An adjective can also come after the person or thing. Then you need am, is or are.
steps.body: *Rina sibuk* is a full sentence in Indonesian, but an English sentence always needs a verb. With no action, **am / is / are** does that job: **Rina is busy.** (She's = She is.) Don't put **a** before an adjective on its own: **She is tired**, not 'She is a tired'. **a** means 'one' and needs a noun: She is **a** tired **teacher**.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Tell a friend about your parents.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Orang tuaku senang.
question.explanation: **My parents** = they (more than one person), so we use **are**, and the adjective **happy** comes after it. Indonesian *Orang tuaku senang* has no word for are, but English needs it.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You're eating at a warung in Jakarta, but your soto isn't hot any more.

question.explanation: English needs **is** before the adjective: **The soto is cold.** Don't use **a** before an adjective on its own: **a** means 'one (thing)', and *cold* isn't a thing.

steps.title: very and really
steps.text: Now let's make adjectives stronger.
steps.body: Put **very** or **really** right **before** the adjective: **very hot, really cheap**. With a noun: **a very small room**. Indonesian *sekali* comes after (*panas sekali*), but **very** comes before. Before a verb (an action word like *like*), use only **really**: I **really like** it, never 'I very like it'. You can also say I like it **very much**: that pair goes at the end.

steps.title: Stronger sentences
steps.text: Here are very and really in everyday sentences. Look at where they go.

examples.en: Bandung is very cold at night.
examples.id: Bandung dingin sekali di malam hari.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You try Rina's rendang. You love it!

question.prompt: What do you say to Rina?
question.explanation: **like** is a verb (an action word), and only **really** can go before a verb: **I really like it!** **very** only makes describing words stronger (very hot, very big), so 'very like' is wrong.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: You see a new car in a showroom in Jakarta. Look at the price!

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ini mobil yang sangat mahal.
question.solution: This is a very expensive car.
question.explanation: The order is **a + very + adjective + noun**: **a very expensive car**. Why **a** and not *an*? a/an looks at the very next word, and here that's **very** (a 'v' sound). Without very it's **an** expensive car.

steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in the patterns.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · adjectives & very
artifact.intro: Where adjectives go, and how to make them stronger.
rows: a red car / an old bike
tips: Indonesian puts the adjective after the noun (*mobil merah*); English puts it **before**: **a red car**.
a/an looks at the very next word: **an** old house, but **a very** old house.
After a person or thing, don't forget **am / is / are**: **She's tired**, not 'She tired'.
**very** goes before adjectives only. Before a verb use **really**: **I really like it**.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar mendeskripsikan orang, tempat dan benda: a red car, a busy day, a very hot afternoon. Yuk, kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Kata sifat di depan
steps.text: Kata sifat adalah kata untuk mendeskripsikan, seperti big, new dan cheap. Yuk lihat posisinya.
steps.body: **Kata sifat** (adjective) menjelaskan sesuatu (big, red, cheap). **Kata benda** (noun) adalah nama benda, orang atau tempat (car, bag, Rina). Dalam bahasa Indonesia kata sifat ada **setelah** kata benda: *mobil merah*. Dalam bahasa Inggris ada **sebelum**: **a red car**. **a/an** melihat bunyi kata tepat sesudahnya: **a** new bike, **an** old bike. Kata sifat tidak pernah diberi **-s**; hanya kata bendanya yang menunjukkan 'lebih dari satu': two **big boxes**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu sedang belanja di pasar di Bandung.

question.prompt: Kamu mau bilang 'Saya mau tas hitam.' Kalimat mana yang benar?
question.explanation: Dalam bahasa Inggris kata sifat ada **sebelum** kata benda: **a black bag**. 'a bag black' memakai urutan bahasa Indonesia. Dan 'blacks' salah: hanya kata benda yang bisa diberi -s, kata sifat tidak pernah.

steps.title: be + kata sifat
steps.text: Kata sifat juga bisa ada setelah orang atau benda. Kalau begitu, kamu butuh am, is atau are.
steps.body: *Rina sibuk* sudah kalimat lengkap dalam bahasa Indonesia, tapi kalimat bahasa Inggris selalu butuh kata kerja. Kalau tidak ada kegiatan, **am / is / are** yang mengisinya: **Rina is busy.** (She's = She is.) Jangan taruh **a** sebelum kata sifat yang berdiri sendiri: **She is tired**, bukan 'She is a tired'. **a** artinya 'satu' dan butuh kata benda: She is **a** tired **teacher**.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Ceritakan tentang orang tuamu kepada teman.

question.explanation: **My parents** = they (lebih dari satu orang), jadi pakai **are**, lalu kata sifat **happy** ada setelahnya. *Orang tuaku senang* tidak punya kata untuk are, tapi bahasa Inggris membutuhkannya.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu makan di warung di Jakarta, tapi sotomu sudah tidak panas lagi.

question.explanation: Bahasa Inggris butuh **is** sebelum kata sifat: **The soto is cold.** Jangan pakai **a** sebelum kata sifat yang berdiri sendiri: **a** artinya 'satu (benda)', dan *cold* bukan benda.

steps.title: very dan really
steps.text: Sekarang kita buat kata sifat jadi lebih kuat.
steps.body: Taruh **very** atau **really** tepat **sebelum** kata sifat: **very hot, really cheap**. Dengan kata benda: **a very small room**. *Sekali* dalam bahasa Indonesia ada di belakang (*panas sekali*), tapi **very** di depan. Sebelum kata kerja (kata kegiatan seperti *like*), pakai hanya **really**: I **really like** it, jangan 'I very like it'. Kamu juga bisa bilang I like it **very much**: pasangan ini ada di akhir.

steps.title: Kalimat yang lebih kuat
steps.text: Ini very dan really dalam kalimat sehari-hari. Perhatikan posisinya.
steps.body: **very / really + kata sifat**, dan **really + kata kerja**.

examples.en: Bandung is very cold at night.
examples.id: Bandung dingin sekali di malam hari.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu mencoba rendang buatan Rina. Enak sekali!

question.prompt: Apa yang kamu katakan kepada Rina?
question.explanation: **like** adalah kata kerja (kata kegiatan), dan hanya **really** yang bisa ada sebelum kata kerja: **I really like it!** **very** hanya menguatkan kata sifat (very hot, very big), jadi 'very like' salah.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Kamu melihat mobil baru di showroom di Jakarta. Lihat harganya!

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ini mobil yang sangat mahal.
question.solution: This is a very expensive car.
question.explanation: Urutannya **a + very + kata sifat + kata benda**: **a very expensive car**. Kenapa **a**, bukan *an*? a/an melihat kata tepat sesudahnya, dan di sini itu **very** (bunyi 'v'). Tanpa very jadi **an** expensive car.

steps.title: Ulasan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini supaya polanya makin melekat.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · kata sifat & very
artifact.intro: Posisi kata sifat, dan cara membuatnya lebih kuat.
rows: a red car / an old bike
a + very + kata sifat + kata benda
tips: Bahasa Indonesia menaruh kata sifat setelah kata benda (*mobil merah*); bahasa Inggris menaruhnya **sebelum**: **a red car**.
a/an melihat kata tepat sesudahnya: **an** old house, tapi **a very** old house.
Setelah orang atau benda, jangan lupa **am / is / are**: **She's tired**, bukan 'She tired'.
**very** hanya sebelum kata sifat. Sebelum kata kerja pakai **really**: **I really like it**.
